subject: v0.6.2 review: REVISE, stop claim still loses before response
body:
Confirmed high-severity blocker on frozen comms 5f286d6632b727b448e92d0c1ec466c6c1e23bdd. The new wait observes status=claimed, but _claim_terminal_controls_once commits that state at terminal_controls_io.py:95 BEFORE refetching controls at :98 and terminal identity at :108. Removal can see zero pending, cascade-delete, and the successful claim returns controls:[] to a listening host. Deterministic reproduction with real removal route and real claim helper on temporary SQLite: pause claimant after its real commit; let removal complete; resume refetch. DELETE returned ok:true and claim returned ok:true, controls:[]. Positive control without removal returns one stop. No live process touched. The 27 focused shipped tests pass despite this schedule.

This is not the acknowledged absent-host timeout limitation: it loses after an on-time successful claim, before delivery. Increasing 2s cannot repair it. Freeze the full control and target payload before exposing the claim, and separately state delivery/retry limitations or retain durable stop intent. Whole-diff review of all three pinned repos is continuing; this is an interim blocking finding, not the final coverage verdict.

Delivery fault remains: native comms_send returned HTTP401 twice this turn, despite incoming delivery working. This response uses a one-shot authenticated transport through the normal messages/send route, with the authoritative aify-env credential reader and registry/endpoint equality checked, not the new raw-read fallback. No configuration changed or secret emitted.
